original_target.title: Boundary-pole decay of the pluricomplex Green function

full_original_statement:
Let $`\Omega\subset\mathbb C^n`$, $`n\ge2`$, be a bounded hyperconvex domain: there exists a negative plurisubharmonic exhaustion $`\rho`$, with $`\{\rho<c\}\Subset\Omega`$ for every $`c<0`$. Define

```math
g_\Omega(z,w)=\sup\{u(z):u\in\mathrm{PSH}(\Omega),\ u\le0,\ \limsup_{s\to w}(u(s)-\log\|s-w\|)<\infty\}.
```

For every nonempty compact $`K\Subset\Omega`$ and every sequence $`w_j\in\Omega`$ with $`\mathrm{dist}(w_j,\partial\Omega)\to0`$, must

```math
\sup_{z\in K}|g_\Omega(z,w_j)|\longrightarrow0?
```

sources.scope_comparison: The actual theorem for arbitrary bounded hyperconvex domains gives Lp decay for every finite p. This does not imply the requested compact-uniform decay of the negative Green function when its pole approaches a rough boundary. Boundary-zero statements fix the pole and move the evaluation point. Extra exhaustion/boundary assumptions in located papers are not allowed here.
